description: A very unsatisfactory site discovered by antiquarians in 1689. Apparently a  sub-circular brick structure from the corner of Whitehorse lane and Jewry lane, located within the area of the Roman forum. Apparently associated with a great many finds the antiquarian recorder considered to be 'votive'. including 1400 - 1500 Roman coins, and 'sacrificial' animal bones.
bibliography: Fulford, M. “Links with the Past: Pervasive ‘ritual’ Behaviour in Roman Britain.” Briitannia 32 (2001): 201.
Urry, W. “A Circular Roman Temple Discovered in the Late Seventeenth Century at Canterbury.” Archaeologia Cantiana 94 (1978): 1–6.
